holidays.name: National Ice Cream Sandwich Day
holidays.description: Today is for the freezer-aisle classic: creamy ice cream between two soft chocolate cookie wafers. Eat it fast, because it melts quickly, and expect sticky fingers. It's a good excuse to have dessert in the sun.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance, and the exact person who started it is unclear. It fits August's run of ice cream days. The treat itself became hugely popular in the early 1900s, when pushcart vendors sold them in American cities.
holidays.funFact: Early ice cream sandwiches were sold from New York City street carts for about a penny. They were a cheap way to cool off, and they were handheld long before the modern freezer case.

holidays.name: National Coloring Book Day
holidays.description: Grab your crayons, markers or colored pencils and go outside the lines. This day celebrates coloring for kids and adults alike. It's a low-pressure way to unwind and be creative, and you don't need any artistic skill.
holidays.origin: The day was introduced by Dover Publications, a long-time publisher of coloring books for children and adults. They created it to promote the relaxing, creative pastime.
holidays.funFact: Adult coloring books became a huge trend in the 2010s. Many people use them as a screen-free way to relax, and some books sold millions of copies.
